meta.title: Glaux — Local AI Workspace
meta.description: Glaux is a local AI workspace for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Chat, read files, and transcribe audio on your computer with any open-weights Safetensors or GGUF model — nothing is sent to a cloud AI.

hero.title: Your AI workspace, on your computer
hero.lede: Chat, read files, and transcribe audio on your machine — nothing is sent to a cloud AI.
hero.claim: Runs any open-weights model in Safetensors or GGUF format.

models.title: Any open-weights model, ready to run
models.body: Pick a model from Hugging Face, download it through Glaux, and start using it. If it is published as Safetensors or GGUF, Glaux can serve it locally — chat, vision, and speech included. No need to tinker around or set up extra software; Glaux manages everything for you.
models.safetensorsBody: The standard weights format on Hugging Face. Use it when you want the complete open-weights model for chatting, looking at images, or transcribing speech.
models.ggufBody: Smaller packaged versions of the same open models. Choose a GGUF build when you want capable AI that fits more comfortably on your machine.
models.note: Some Hub models are gated. Accept the license on the model page, then set a Hugging Face access token in your environment before you open Glaux.

uses.title: Everyday work, kept private
uses.lead: Glaux is a workspace for people who want local AI for writing, files, and recordings — not a developer toolkit.
uses.chatBody: Draft emails, outline ideas, and talk through a problem the way you would with a cloud assistant — except the conversation stays on your computer. Sessions are saved in your workspace so you can pick up later.
uses.photosTitle: Ask about what is in an image
uses.photosBody: Drop a photo or screenshot into the chat when the model supports images. Describe a scene, extract text from a picture, or ask what is happening — useful for receipts, whiteboards, and everyday snapshots.
uses.audioBody: Attach a voice memo, meeting recording, or video. Glaux can transcribe the audio on your machine so you get a written record without sending the file to a transcription service.
uses.pdfsBody: PDFs are turned into readable text automatically. Drop in an invoice, form, or report and ask for totals, names, or a short summary — the file never leaves your workspace.
uses.projectsTitle: Keep work in its own workspace
uses.projectsBody: Each workspace has its own chats, resource library, and outputs. Switch workspaces when you change projects so files and conversations do not mix.

features.title: A full workspace, not just a chat box
features.lead: Everything you need to download a model, talk to it, and keep the files that come out of that work.
features.localChatBody: Conversations run on your computer. Nothing is sent to a cloud AI for inference.
features.openModelsBody: Download and run Safetensors or GGUF models from Hugging Face directly through Glaux.
features.filesBody: Attach files in chat when the selected model can use them. Simply drag and drop them into your message.
features.pdfBody: Documents are parsed automatically so you can search, quote, and ask questions about them.
features.transcriptionBody: Turn recordings and video soundtracks into text with a speech model from the Hub.
features.switchBody: Change models during a session in order to mix and match capabilities as you need them and keep the conversation.
features.workspacesBody: Separate projects, each with its own resource library, sessions, and outputs.
features.sessionsBody: Chats persist on disk. Search them, reopen them, and export or delete individual messages.
features.resourcesBody: Keep the files a project needs in one place, with drag-and-drop and a built-in markdown editor.
features.outputsBody: Find generated and exported files next to the chat, ready to open or copy back into your resource library.
features.themeBody: Follows your system by default. Switch to light or dark any time from the theme selector in the header.
features.platformsBody: One desktop app per platform. GPU is used automatically when your machine has one.

how.title: From install to first conversation
how.lead: You do not need any prior experience running AI models. Simply follow these steps in the app to get started.
how.s1Body: Download the installer for your system, run it, and launch Glaux from the Start menu, Applications, or your desktop shortcut. No extra runtimes to install.
how.s2Body: The header shows the active workspace. Stay on Default, or create a new one for a project. Each workspace keeps its own chats and files.
how.s3Body: In the Models panel, paste a Hugging Face model id such as org/model-name and choose Add. Glaux fetches any open-weights Safetensors or GGUF model you pick. For GGUF you can choose a smaller or larger variant before the download starts.
how.s4Body: Click the downloaded model to load it. Type in the input field at the bottom of the chat window and send. A context meter shows how much of the model’s memory the conversation is using.
how.s5Title: Drop in files when you need them
how.s5Body: Drag images, audio, video, or PDFs into your message in order to pass them to the model. Use a vision model for pictures, a speech model for recordings, or attach a PDF to ask about the document.
how.s6Body: Sessions holds past conversations. Resources is your project library. Outputs collects files you export or generate. Everything is saved under your user profile on your computer.

privacy.title: Chats, files, and models stay with you at all times
privacy.body: Glaux runs models on your computer. Sessions, resources, and outputs live in your user profile. Model files are stored on disk after you download them — they are not uploaded for someone else to host. If your machine has a compatible GPU, Glaux uses it automatically; otherwise it falls back to the CPU.

download.title: Install the desktop app
download.lead: The current public installer is for Windows. Models are downloaded after you install — they are not inside the setup file. A GPU driver helps when you want faster responses, but it is not required.
download.noteWindows: Windows 10 or 11. Run the setup, choose a folder if you like, then open Glaux from the Start menu.
download.noteMac: macOS packaging is supported, but the currently published installer is for Windows. Check Releases for newer builds.
download.noteLinux: Linux packaging is supported, but the currently published installer is for Windows. Check Releases for newer builds.
